description: Scaffold the Next.js 14 project with Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, and global styling. Set up the foundational dark-mode theme, typography, and layout structure.
steps: Initialize a Next.js 14 project with TypeScript and App Router in /projects/sandbox/dev using pnpm (run: pnpm create next-app@latest . --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir=false --import-alias='@/*' --use-pnpm) - answer yes to all prompts or use flags to skip prompts

Configure tailwind.config.ts with the custom theme: extend colors with 'neon' (#E4F12D), 'dark' (#000000), 'charcoal' (#111111). Add custom font families for headings (font-heading: extended bold sans-serif like 'Oswald' or similar from Google Fonts) and body (font-body: 'Inter' or similar clean sans-serif).

Set up app/layout.tsx with: dark background (bg-black text-white), import Google Fonts (Oswald for headings, Inter for body), metadata with title 'Portfolio | Brand Hub', and wrap children in a main layout container.
Set up app/globals.css with Tailwind directives, custom CSS variables for the theme colors, smooth scroll behavior, and any base reset styles needed for the dark theme.
Create app/page.tsx as the main page that will import and render all section components (placeholder divs for now with section names).
Verify the project builds with pnpm build and the dev server starts.
acceptance_criteria: The page renders with a black background and white text by default
Tailwind config includes neon, dark, and charcoal colors
Google Fonts (or system fonts as fallback) are configured for headings and body
